content.value_statement: Async database code can be hard to structure correctly. This skill gives SQLAlchemy 2.0 patterns for typed models, sessions, queries, and API integration.
actual_capabilities: Shows async engine and session factory setup for SQLAlchemy 2.0.
Demonstrates typed ORM models with mapped columns and relationships.
Provides async CRUD examples for create, read, and update workflows.
Explains eager loading, pagination, aggregations, and streaming result sets.
Shows FastAPI dependency injection patterns for async sessions.
Documents database URLs and package choices for common async drivers.
limitations: It is documentation only and does not execute or validate generated code.
It does not provide complete migration project scaffolding.
It uses placeholder database credentials that must be replaced.
It does not cover production retry, timeout, or observability policies.

use_cases.title: Build async API storage
use_cases.description: Create SQLAlchemy sessions and models for FastAPI services that need clean database access.

use_cases.title: Modernize ORM models
use_cases.description: Move legacy model examples toward SQLAlchemy 2.0 typed mappings and async sessions.

use_cases.title: Tune query loading
use_cases.description: Apply eager loading, pagination, and streaming patterns to reduce query cost and memory use.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic async model
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design an async SQLAlchemy 2.0 User model with an engine, session factory, and simple create function.

prompt_templates.title: Add relationships and loading
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to model Users and Posts with a one-to-many relationship and a query that loads posts efficiently.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate with FastAPI
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a FastAPI database dependency that yields an async session and closes it reliably.

prompt_templates.title: Design read-write routing
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline an AsyncSession routing approach for read replicas and write database connections.

output_examples.input: I need a typed User and Post model for an async API.
output: A typed model structure with primary keys, foreign keys, and relationships.
A session pattern that fits async request handling.
Notes about where to add validation and migrations.

output_examples.input: My endpoint loads posts and authors slowly.
output: A query loading plan that avoids repeated relationship lookups.
A pagination approach for large result sets.
A short checklist for indexes and session boundaries.

output_examples.input: I need to run a custom SQL report safely.
output: A parameterized raw SQL approach for user-supplied values.
A session usage pattern that keeps transaction scope clear.
A reminder to avoid placing secrets in sample database URLs.

best_practices: Use context managers so sessions close after each request or task.
Prefer parameterized SQL expressions when raw SQL is required.
Use eager loading deliberately to prevent repeated relationship queries.
anti_patterns: Do not keep long-lived sessions shared across unrelated requests.
Do not copy placeholder credentials into production configuration.
Do not mix synchronous database sessions into async request handlers.

faq.question: Does this skill run database commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides reference patterns and example prompts; the assistant or user decides what to execute.

faq.question: Which SQLAlchemy version does it target?
faq.answer: It targets SQLAlchemy 2.0 and newer async ORM patterns.

faq.question: Can it help with FastAPI?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes async session dependency patterns suitable for FastAPI routes.

faq.question: Does it include migration tooling?
faq.answer: It mentions Alembic commands, but it does not scaffold a complete migration setup.

faq.question: Are the database URLs real credentials?
faq.answer: No. The URLs use placeholders and must be replaced with secure local configuration.

faq.question: Can it optimize existing queries?
faq.answer: It can suggest eager loading, pagination, aggregation, and streaming patterns from the included examples.
